r-m1-001.q: What is the core difference that allows Deep Learning to overcome the limitations of classical Machine Learning?
r-m1-001.correct: It automatically identifies and extracts the best features from raw data through multi-layer neural networks
wrong: It requires experts to manually design and extract features from raw data
It only works well on small tabular datasets with a limited number of attributes
It relies entirely on fixed if-then rule sets predefined by humans

r-m1-002.q: Which event marked the official recognition of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a field of scientific research?
wrong: Alan Turing's development of the Turing Test (1950)
The invention of the Perceptron algorithm (1957)
The invention of the Backpropagation algorithm (1986)

r-m1-003.q: What was the main cause of the first AI Winter (AI Winter 1) in the 1960s-1970s?
r-m1-003.correct: Funding cuts due to reports on the failure of machine translation (ALPAC) and the limitations of the Perceptron
wrong: The cost of maintaining Expert Systems was too high and they were difficult to scale
The defeat of the Deep Blue supercomputer by chess grandmaster Garry Kasparov
Artificial neural networks could not be scaled up to solve large enterprise problems

r-m1-004.q: When was the Backpropagation algorithm introduced in the history of AI?
r-m1-004.correct: In 1986, during the Expert Systems boom (1980s)
wrong: In 1957, at the same time as the Perceptron algorithm
In 1950, when Alan Turing published the Turing Test
In 2012, at the time of the AlexNet boom

r-m1-005.q: How is Machine Learning precisely defined?
r-m1-005.correct: The study of programs that are not explicitly programmed but learn patterns from data over time
wrong: The branch of science that simulates intelligent behavior in computers to imitate human cognition
A multi-layer neural network model specialized for processing large-scale nonlinear data
A system based on fixed expert rules to make automatic inferences

r-m1-006.q: In the Machine Learning workflow, which step comes immediately after 'Data Collection'?
wrong: Modeling
Validation
Deployment

r-m1-007.q: Among the basic terms of machine learning, how is 'Target' defined?
r-m1-007.correct: The category or value that we are trying to predict
wrong: The data attributes used as explanatory variables for prediction
A single data point corresponding to one row in the data table
The specific target value that has been labeled for each observation

r-m1-008.q: In a Machine Learning model, which component does the term 'Features' refer to?
r-m1-008.correct: The data attributes used for prediction (explanatory variables)
wrong: The target label value that the model must produce as output
A single observation in the test dataset
The residual error between predicted and actual results

r-m1-009.q: What is a single data point in a data table (usually corresponding to one row) called?
wrong: Feature
Target
Label

r-m1-010.q: What harm do duplicate data in the training set cause to the model?
r-m1-010.correct: They bias the weights during training
wrong: They cause the model to always underfit due to a lack of data
They make categorical variables impossible to convert with One-hot encoding
They automatically remove outlier observations in the test set

r-m1-011.q: Which values does Imputation typically use as replacements when handling missing data?
r-m1-011.correct: The mean, median, or most frequent value
wrong: A fixed value of 0 or the largest outlier value of the attribute
A random value from any normal distribution unrelated to the dataset
The Euclidean distance between the two farthest observations

r-m1-012.q: What method is the Masking technique understood to be in handling missing data?
r-m1-012.correct: Creating a separate category for missing values
wrong: Completely deleting rows or columns that contain missing values
Mathematical interpolation based on the nearest neighboring data points
Normalizing the data to the range [0, 1] before training

r-m1-013.q: Which visualization chart is mentioned in the material as helping to detect outliers?
wrong: Histogram
Scatter plot
Pair plot

r-m1-014.q: What is the main purpose of conducting Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) before building a model?
r-m1-014.correct: To gain a preliminary understanding of the data and identify patterns and trends before modeling
wrong: To optimize the hyperparameters of the classification algorithm
To prune decision tree branches in order to reduce variance
To generate synthetic samples for an imbalanced minority class

r-m1-015.q: Among EDA visualization techniques, what is a Scatter plot mainly used for?
r-m1-015.correct: Observing the relationship between two quantitative variables
wrong: Observing the shape of the frequency distribution of a single variable
Displaying the multivariate correlation matrix of all variables at once
Detecting misclassified label errors in the test set

r-m1-016.q: Which chart is preferred for examining multivariate correlations among many pairs of attributes at once in EDA?
wrong: Histogram
Box plot
A single Scatter plot

r-m1-017.q: What is the main effect of the Log Transformation in feature engineering?
r-m1-017.correct: It makes skewed data more closely resemble a normal distribution, which is useful for Linear Regression
wrong: It converts categorical data into binary variables 0 or 1
It increases the dimensionality of the feature space using powers of 2 and 3
It generates new data points to balance the proportions of the classification classes

r-m1-018.q: One-hot encoding is most suitable for which type of categorical variable?
wrong: Ordinal (categories with a hierarchical order)
Continuous (continuous numeric variables with negative values)
Discrete (countable integer variables)

r-m1-019.q: In which case should Ordinal encoding be applied instead of One-hot encoding?
r-m1-019.correct: When the categorical variable has a clear order (Ordinal), assigning numeric values in the order 1, 2, 3...
wrong: When the categorical variable has no ranking whatsoever (Nominal)
When the data contains many outliers and needs to be noise-resistant
When one wants to transform skewed data into a normal distribution

r-m1-020.q: Which scaling method uses the interquartile range and is more robust to outliers?
wrong: Min-Max Scaling
Standard Scaling
One-hot Encoding

r-m1-021.q: Standard Scaling transforms data to a standard distribution with which values of the mean and standard deviation (std)?
wrong: mean = 0, std = 0
mean = 1, std = 1
mean = 0.5, std = 0.5

r-m1-022.q: What is the core difference between Estimation and Inference in statistics?
r-m1-022.correct: Estimation applies an algorithm to compute a value, whereas inference determines the accuracy of that estimate
wrong: Estimation is used for non-parametric models, whereas inference is used for parametric models
Estimation is computed on the test set, whereas inference is performed only on the training set
Estimation updates the posterior distribution, whereas inference only repeats independent trials

r-m1-023.q: What is the main characteristic of a Parametric model?
r-m1-023.correct: It assumes the data follow a specific distribution (e.g., the Normal distribution)
wrong: It makes no assumptions at all about the probability distribution of the data
It only stores the entire training data and defers computation until prediction time
It always uses a number of parameters that grows in proportion to the number of data samples

r-m1-024.q: Which of the following examples is given in the material as representing a Non-parametric method?
wrong: The Normal distribution
Classical Linear Regression
The Bernoulli binomial distribution

r-m1-025.q: How does the Bayesian view of statistical inference differ from the Frequentist school?
r-m1-025.correct: It describes parameters through probability distributions and updates beliefs from the prior to the posterior as data are observed
wrong: It focuses only on frequency of occurrence through infinitely repeated trials
It treats the parameter as always a single fixed constant that cannot have a distribution
It absolutely does not use prior probability information in the inference process
